BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or

timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each

each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several positions would also move us outside our own authority limits, such as the 20% cap and 18-month period, which we cannot accept without Amelia Frost's written approval. The seller's documents are also described as "negotiated" and "settled," but nothing in the file shows that we agreed to them. I'd treat them as opening positions, not as agreed terms.

## 1. Liability architecture

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl. 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m opening; 20% only as conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft | Reject. We have no authority to accept 20%. Counter at 25%. |
| De minimis (cl. 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. A 25k de minimis would exclude many real claims. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, then recovery of excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, then first-dollar recovery (tipping) | Reject. This is five times our basket, and the excess-only mechanic removes the first AUD 250k of losses entirely. |
| General claims period (cl. 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval | Reject. 18 months needs her approval, which we don't have. |
| Universal limitation clause | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This is a hidden override that would pull Title, Tax, IP, and fraud into the general regime. |

**Reasoning:** The seller's package isn't a minor variation. Taken together (a higher de minimis, a much larger basket, an excess-only deductible, a shorter period, and a cap that applies to everything), it would substantially reduce our recourse on general warranty claims. The "universal limitation" wording is the most dangerous point because it is drafted to override the category structure.

## 2. Fundamental / Title claims

The seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as the general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

**Reject.** Our playbook requires a separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar. Title is the core of what we are buying (100% of the shares). Putting it under a 20% cap and 18-month period would leave us exposed if the seller's title is defective. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to weaken title protection.

## 3. Exclusions, reliance, and fraud

- **Cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5:** Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out. **Reject.** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this, and our team cannot agree otherwise.

## 4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

- **Disclosure letter 1.1 and 1.2:** The seller discloses everything in the data room (as at 5pm 22 September 2026) and all public registers and statutory records. **Reject.** Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure. Blanket data-room and public-register disclosure would make almost any issue "disclosed" against us, including matters we cannot realistically find. The disclosure letter's own wording ("without limiting any specific disclosure") also shows that the general disclosure is intended to operate as a catch-all.
- **Cl. 8.3 (buyer knowledge):** The buyer has no claim for anything "known" to the buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." **Reject.** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must name specific seller knowledge persons, require reasonable enquiry by the seller, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud, or a specific indemnity.

## 5. Specific transaction issues

### Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30%)
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure letter (section 2):** The seller has *not* yet included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that conditions in cl. 11.3 are satisfied.
- **Assessment:** The seller's own disclosure confirms the consent isn't in hand. Under our playbook, "reasonable endeavours" is not enough for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.
- **Push back:** Require an effective written consent *and* evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent. The purchase price should not be paid until this is met.

### Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding)
- **Seller position:** A release to be provided after Completion.
- **Disclosure letter (section 3):** The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- **Assessment:** A post-completion release leaves the company's assets encumbered after we have paid for them, and gives us no leverage if the bank does not release.
- **Push back:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. If any release has to come afterwards, it requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

### Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)
- **Seller position:** The bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure letter (section 5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and it is not stated whether payroll tax, super, or on-costs apply.
- **Assessment:** Silently leaving AUD 420,000 out of the funds flow means the cost could land on the company (and us) after Completion. The on-costs are unquantified.
- **Push back:** Add the bonuses as a specific funds flow line item, or make them expressly seller-funded, with on-costs included. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### Ironquay IP
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure letter (section 4):** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 project materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, but this is not bank-verified either way. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Assessment:** The narrow indemnity does not address the transfer risk. We have no evidence on whether the AUD 180,000 is actually owed.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer defects, preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as established, either as owed or as paid. Verify independently. Tax and IP terms remain open; do not agree to resolve them here.

### Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Disclosure letter (section 6):** A download link went to an unintended external address; around 1,240 records may be affected. Whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, and whether notification is required are all unresolved. The disclosure does not characterise this as a confirmed breach.
- **Assessment:** We should not characterise it as a breach, nor assume harm or a notification duty. But "not expected to be material" is the seller's conclusion, not a finding, and the investigation is still open.
- **Push back:** Require log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular written updates. Ask for a specific indemnity or a clear allocation of the costs of any notification, investigation, or regulatory response, without assuming any figure. Make sure the incident sits outside the general regime, not under the seller's proposed limitations.

### Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure letter (section 8):** The three renewals (AUD 110,000 each) have not been characterised as unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or ordinary-course.
- **Assessment:** The seller's characterisation is unsupported. We should assess the renewals on their terms. Our playbook says no automatic debt classification or price deduction, so we shouldn't reclassify them as debt, but we also shouldn't accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence.
- **Push back:** Request the contracts and their terms, and clarify timing and whether they are terminable. Assess before making any price proposal.

### Title
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by" the company share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure letter (section 10):** DD-012 is the source relied on, and the seller has not stated that the buyer has verified title itself.
- **Assessment:** DD-012 is a seller-supplied internal register, not independent proof. It does not establish encumbrances or authority.
- **Push back:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance, and authority evidence (for example, searches, a statutory declaration, or a verified ASIC extract with a chain of transfer), plus the title protection described above.

### Other items the seller raised
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation identified, but the disclosure doesn't say landlord consent is required for the share sale. Ask the seller to confirm this in writing and provide the lease clause.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; the provision does not say consent is needed for a share sale. Ask for legal confirmation that no consent is required, or get the consent.

## 6. Tax and IP positions

The seller says the tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime." **Reject.** Our playbook says these terms remain open, and we should not assume unlimited liability or resolve them. Putting tax and IP under the general 20% cap and 18-month period would be a hidden override. Keep them as separate categories and flag them for specialist tax and IP input before we agree anything.

## 7. Authority constraints

- The 20% cap and the 18-month claims period are both fallbacks that require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- Do not reply to the seller in a way that accepts either point, even provisionally, until that approval exists.
- Any concession on these points needs her approval first.

## 8. Recommendations (summary)

**Priority 1: Walk-away-level points (must fix)**
1. Reject the universal limitation clause and restore category separation. Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant, and fraud sit in separate regimes.
2. Add a fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance.
3. Restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket and de minimis.
4. Reject whole-data-room and public-register disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
5. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. Make Bluefen consent an effective pre-Completion condition, with evidence that its conditions are met.
7. Require Riverlark payout and security release at Completion.

**Priority 2: Economic terms**
8. Counter the cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m.
9. Counter the de minimis at AUD 5,000 and the basket at AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
10. Counter the general claims period at 24 months.
11. Add the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs to the funds flow as a line item or seller-funded.

**Priority 3: Specific indemnities and diligence**
12. Broaden the Ironquay IP indemnity, keeping the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
13. Obtain logs, investigation updates, and a cost allocation for the DD-006 incident, without assuming a breach or any figure.
14. Request the Sandbar contracts; assess before making any price proposal.
15. Obtain independent title evidence beyond DD-012.
16. Obtain written confirmation on the office lease and Mossvale consent points.

**Priority 4: Process**
17. Keep tax and IP open and get specialist input.
18. Do not accept the 20% cap or 18-month period without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
19. Respond to the seller treating their documents as opening positions, not agreed terms.

I haven't reviewed the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012) directly. My assessment relies on the seller's summaries of them, so the buyer team should check those summaries against the source material before finalising the mark-up.
